articles.headline: If FIFA expands the World Cup again, how would a 64-team tournament work?
articles.description: The 2026 World Cup was the first to feature 48 teams, and 2030 could see the field swell to 64, but just how feasible is a tournament that size?

articles.headline: Pochettino shares 'regret' over Balogun controversy, impact on USMNT
articles.description: USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino said he regrets not being more involved in the process of appealing Folarin Balogun's suspension at this summer's World Cup, adding that the incident changed the energy around his squad.

articles.headline: Can Patrick Vieira rescue Senegal from their post-AFCON final hellscape?
articles.description: Senegal, surely, must be asking what on earth they have done to receive the misfortune and wretched experiences they've endured since January, when they won, and then lost, the AFCON final.

articles.headline: Premier League, LaLiga, Serie A, Bundesliga demand FIFA reform amid Gianni Infantino re-election bid
articles.description: The top leagues in England, Italy, Germany and Spain have issued a joint-statement demanding governance reform at FIFA, amid Gianni Infantino's bid to be re-elected as president in 2027.

articles.headline: Gianni Infantino says he is 'committed to doing what is right' for FIFA
articles.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino says he has "never been more determined and committed" to doing "what is right for the game" after pledging to conduct an independent review of the organisation's governance.
